newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Turkey's military chief begins Israel visit.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's military chief begins Israel visit.

text.p: The chief of Turkey's armed forces, General Ismail Hakki Karadayi, began a three-day visit to Israel on Monday in a further sign of strengthening military cooperation between the two countries.

"I believe that my visit will contribute towards further development of the expanding relations between our two armies," Karadayi was quoted as saying in an interview with Israel's Haaretz newspaper before travelling to the Jewish state.
"I will hold talks with Israeli officials of various ranks on regional security and cooperation," Haaretz quoted him as saying.

Karadayi was due to meet Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai and Israeli army chief Amnon Shahak, as well as tour military bases during the visit which began with a tour of Jerusalem's Yad Vashem Holocaust memorial.

Moslem but secular Turkey and Israel have signed two military accords, which involve allowing Israeli jets on training flights in Turkish airspace and upgrading of the Turkish Air Force's fleet of F-4 Phantom jets by Israel. The accords were condemned by Iran and many in the Arab world.

Ankara's closer links with Israel also drew strong protests at the time from Islamists in Turkey. Since becoming prime minister eight months ago Islamist Welfare Party leader Necmettin Erbakan has toned down his criticism.
However, a Welfare mayor was detained by police earlier this month after organising an anti-Israel protest near Ankara.
Asked by Haaretz if he feared his visit would anger Turkish Islamists, Karadayi said: "The secular and democratic structure of the Turkish republic is anchored in the constitution and cannot change."
He said Turkey aspired "to develop relations with Israel as well as with all the countries in the region."
Israel and Turkey, the army chief told Haaretz, are "the only democracies in the region and both have a similar approach towards security problems".
